summary: isdecimal returns True only for a nonempty string consisting entirely of Unicode decimal digits.
documentation: isdecimal returns True only for a nonempty string consisting entirely of Unicode decimal digits. Signs, decimal points and whitespace are not decimal-digit characters.
caution: Unicode decimal digits include more than ASCII 0–9. Use a different explicit rule when an external format requires ASCII only.
scenarios: Check whether a supplied label contains decimal digits only.
Recognize Unicode decimal text before a separate conversion step.
Separate digit-only reference values from references with signs or letters.
title: Recognize decimal-digit text
problem: Input is a string. Return True exactly when Python isdecimal returns True. Accept Unicode decimal digits, but reject an empty string, signs, spaces, decimal points and superscript digits.
goal: Use str.isdecimal() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Use isdecimal; isdigit accepts some extra digit characters.
